stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image support.

stories.title: Universal Music is launching an AI music platform with ElevenLabs
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Universal Music Group is launching a new AI music platform.
The platform will enable users to create remixes and mashups using licensed music from the UMG catalog.
The development is a multiyear licensing partnership with ElevenLabs, a specialized AI company.

stories.title: Forgejo <=16.0.3 Critical RCE
stories.author: weierstass
bullet_points: A critical Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability has been discovered in Forgejo.
The affected versions of the software are those less than or equal to 16.0.3.
This is a high-severity security flaw requiring immediate patching by users of Forgejo.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, indicating a focus on model deployment.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The model is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key AI/ML domains including transformers and text-generation.
The mention of 'llama' and 'safetensors' indicates relevance to modern large language model deployment.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for persistent AI agents.
The model is designed for complex, multi-step tasks, context gathering, and tool calling on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The speed improvement is attributed to the use of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to 90% faster performance according to the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using its MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model responses.
The updated engine also delivers faster response times and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new large language model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents can run entirely on the user's local hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Electric air taxis get the green light for test flights in Texas
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: A new federal program is launching in Texas to test electric, hybrid-electric, and autonomous aircraft.
The testing initiative precedes the finalization of regulatory rules for this emerging technology.
The FAA's Advanced Air Mobility and eVTOL Integration Pilot Program (eIPP) has selected eight state-led participants.

stories.title: Panic builds over bankrupt Spirit’s looming data sale to Google
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Spirit Airlines' bankruptcy proceedings are linked to a potential data sale to Google.
The news raises concerns about the commodification of personal data during corporate distress.
The article frames the situation as a warning against 'bankruptcy becoming the new land grab for AI.'

stories.title: Six Chinese AI firms accused of aggressively copying US frontier models
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Six Chinese AI firms are accused of aggressively copying US frontier AI models.
The US is reportedly urging AI companies to identify and secretly downgrade Chinese users to less capable models.
The story highlights escalating geopolitical tensions surrounding AI technology and intellectual property.

stories.title: Show-Harness: Just a VLM Agent Can Play Robots
stories.author: Mike Zheng Shou
bullet_points: Introduces Show-Harness, an Embodied Harness designed to bridge the gap between high-level VLM intelligence and low-level robot control.
The system allows Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to 'play' robots by reasoning over discrete semantic action units.
Embodiment-specific interpreters deterministically translate these semantic intents into actionable, local robot commands.

stories.title: ConvMem: Convolutional Memory for Long-Context Reasoning
stories.author: Bo Xu
bullet_points: Addresses the context length limitation of Large Language Models (LLMs) for long-context reasoning.
Proposes 'ConvMem,' a convolutional memory approach to overcome the latency and RL training costs of sequential memory methods (like MemAgent).
Focuses on improving LLM efficiency and capability when processing extremely long inputs without relying on costly iterative updates.

stories.title: Forgetting Only What Matters: Layer-Selective Unlearning toward Robust LLMs
stories.author: Agoritsa Polyzou
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of LLM memorization of sensitive or undesirable training data.
Proposes 'Layer-Selective Unlearning' as a targeted alternative to costly full model retraining.
Aims to improve the robustness of unlearning methods against deployment changes like quantization.

stories.title: ConvMem: Convolutional Memory for Long-Context Reasoning
stories.author: Bo Xu
bullet_points: Addresses the context length limitation of Large Language Models (LLMs).
Proposes 'ConvMem,' a convolutional memory approach to handle long-context reasoning.
Aims to overcome the high latency and costly RL training associated with sequential memory methods.

stories.title: From Symbolic Perception to Logical Deduction: A Framework for Guiding Language Models in Geometric Reasoning
stories.author: Yi Zhou
bullet_points: Proposes a framework to enhance LLMs for geometric reasoning, addressing a known AI challenge.
The method integrates a 'Geometric Vision Parser' to translate visual diagrams into a format LLMs can process.
The framework aims to match or exceed state-of-the-art Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) while potentially offering computational advantages.

stories.title: Rust Is Tier-1 Language at Microsoft
stories.author: rustfoundation.org via mmastrac
bullet_points: Microsoft has officially designated Rust as a Tier-1 language within its development ecosystem.
This indicates a significant strategic commitment by Microsoft to adopting Rust for core infrastructure and development.
The move signals a broader industry trend toward using memory-safe languages like Rust for critical systems.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to leverage open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It enhances Ollama's MLX engine specifically for better performance on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Meta’s Muse AI works and creeps me out
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Meta has released its new AI assistant, Muse, signaling a push into AI-powered productivity tools.
Muse is designed to automate routine tasks such as online shopping, email management, and trip planning.
The article offers a hands-on review, balancing the utility of the tool against user apprehension.

stories.title: How the iPhone Duo compares to other folding phones
stories.author: Brad Bourque
bullet_points: Apple is set to release a foldable phone, dubbed the iPhone Duo, on October 23rd.
The device is priced at $1,999, positioning it competitively against high-end Android foldables like the Pixel 11 Pro Fold and Galaxy Z Fold 8.
The iPhone Duo enters a market previously dominated by Android manufacturers such as Samsung, OnePlus, and Google.

stories.title: Europe will go it alone on Venus mission after NASA yanks radar instrument
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: Europe is pursuing an independent mission to Venus due to NASA's withdrawal of a radar instrument.
The situation highlights potential shifts in international space collaboration, with Europe potentially looking toward China.
The news reflects broader trends of NASA reassessing or canceling existing international partnerships.

stories.title: Android can now securely migrate your logins between password managers
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Android now supports secure migration of login credentials between password managers.
The feature is currently limited in terms of supported applications.
Google has indicated that broader app support for this migration capability is planned.

stories.title: Drones deliver food and remove bodies after Nepal’s flood disaster
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: DJI drones are being utilized in Nepal's flood relief efforts.
The drones are performing critical tasks, including food delivery and body removal.
This leverages existing drone technology, previously used for high-altitude operations like Mount Everest supply.

stories.title: Four groups caught using the same Chrome and Windows exploit kit
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Multiple hacking groups were found utilizing the same exploit kit targeting Chrome and Windows.
The vulnerability exploitation highlights the risk posed by patch gaps in operating systems and browsers.
The accelerated discovery of vulnerabilities, potentially aided by AI, is cited as a contributing factor to the threat landscape.

stories.title: IBIB: A Protocol for Measuring Enterprise AI Systems by Serving Route, Not Model Identifier
stories.author: Brian Sathianathan
bullet_points: Proposes a new protocol (IBIB) to accurately measure enterprise AI systems based on their serving route, rather than just model identifiers.
Addresses the industry problem where current benchmarks only score advertised model identifiers, ignoring crucial deployment factors like serving route and precision.
The protocol includes a preflight check to verify execution contracts and a scoring rule that incorporates reliability.

stories.title: Semigroup-JEPA: Latent Dynamics Consistency for Zero-Shot Physics Generalization
stories.author: John Sous
bullet_points: Introduces SemiGroup-JEPA (SG-JEPA) to enhance Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) world models.
Addresses the limitation of existing JEPA models by incorporating physics parameters into the temporal model via action-conditioning.
Aims to improve the models' ability to learn physics and generate physically realistic dynamics for zero-shot generalization.

stories.title: JarvisGUI: Towards Cross-Device GUI Agents with Dynamic Task Composition
stories.author: Haifeng Wang
bullet_points: Introduces JarvisGUI, a framework aiming to enable cross-device GUI agents.
Addresses a gap in current AI benchmarks by focusing on complex, multi-device workflows.
Highlights the need for agents to manage shared state and coordinate across heterogeneous environments for real-world applicability.

stories.title: Fortunate Recall: Ontology-Driven Memory Lifecycle Management for Persistent Coherence in LLMs
stories.author: Eray Tüzün
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of unbounded memory growth and retrieval degradation in Large Language Models (LLMs).
Introduces 'Fortunate Recall' (FR), a policy layer that manages memory lifecycle based on fact type.
Classifies personal facts into a behavioral ontology (10+1 categories) to apply tailored retention policies like differential temporal decay.

stories.title: Can Foundation Models Moderate Online Content? Evaluating Instruction- vs. Example-Driven Policy Operationalization
stories.author: Abhisek Dash
bullet_points: The paper investigates the reliability of Foundation Models (specifically VLMs) for content moderation.
It compares two methods for guiding models: instruction-driven (reasoning from policy) versus example-driven.
The research addresses the critical industry challenge of consistently operationalizing complex content moderation policies.

stories.title: Cross-Model Agreement as a Deployment-Time Reliability Signal for Automatic Polyp Segmentation
stories.author: Jitin Singla
bullet_points: Addresses a critical real-world problem in medical AI: silent failure of segmentation models during deployment when ground truth is unavailable.
Introduces Referee-Based Quality Estimation (RBQE), a reference-free framework to measure model reliability by comparing a primary model against an independent 'referee' model.
Validated on a standardized external benchmark, indicating practical relevance for deploying robust polyp segmentation in colonoscopy.

stories.title: IBIB: A Protocol for Measuring Enterprise AI Systems by Serving Route, Not Model Identifier
stories.author: Brian Sathianathan
bullet_points: Proposes a new protocol (IBIB) to accurately measure enterprise AI system capabilities.
Addresses the industry problem where current benchmarks only score advertised model identifiers, ignoring deployment specifics like serving route and precision.
The protocol includes a preflight check to verify execution contracts and a reliability-inclusive scoring rule.

stories.title: Learning with Covariance Matrices: Principal Component Analysis Meets Learning with Graphs
stories.author: Alejandro Ribeiro
bullet_points: The paper introduces Covariance Neural Networks (VNNs), which are Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) designed to operate directly on covariance matrices.
This approach leverages the inherent pairwise statistical dependencies within covariance matrices, which are common across various domains.
It addresses a gap in existing GNN theory by accommodating the data-driven nuances of covariance matrices, moving beyond abstract graph representations.

stories.title: Deep Learning-Based Detection of Electrical Faults and Power Quality Disturbances in Aerospace Power Systems
stories.author: Berker Peköz
bullet_points: Addresses the need for fault detection in high-frequency (400 Hz) aerospace power systems, moving beyond traditional 50/60 Hz grid methods.
Introduces a hardware-aware deep learning framework specifically designed for multiclass detection of electrical faults and power quality disturbances.
Utilizes a high-fidelity simulation model based on the Boeing 787 electrical architecture for validation.

stories.title: IBIB: A Protocol for Measuring Enterprise AI Systems by Serving Route, Not Model Identifier
stories.author: Brian Sathianathan
bullet_points: Proposes a new protocol (IBIB) to measure enterprise AI systems based on their serving route rather than just model identifiers.
Highlights a critical industry issue where current benchmarks only test advertised model IDs, ignoring crucial deployment factors like serving route and precision.
The protocol includes a preflight check to verify execution contracts and a scoring rule to account for reliability.

stories.title: Building Multilingual Bridges: Data Mixing as the Pillar of Generalization for In-Language Reasoning
stories.author: Julia Kreutzer
bullet_points: Current reasoning language models exhibit strong English-centric bias, limiting accessibility for non-English speakers.
The research proposes 'Data Mixing' as a core technique to improve multilingual generalization in reasoning models.
The goal is to advance 'L2 reasoning,' enabling models to reason consistently in the language of the prompt.

stories.title: Can Foundation Models Moderate Online Content? Evaluating Instruction- vs. Example-Driven Policy Operationalization
stories.author: Abhisek Dash
bullet_points: Investigates the feasibility of using Foundation Models (VLMs) for consistent online content moderation.
Compares two methods for guiding models: instruction-driven (reasoning from policy precepts) vs. example-driven.
Addresses the critical challenge of operationalizing increasingly complex content moderation policies.

stories.title: Retrofitting Code Using LLMs to Support Exceptional Behavior
stories.author: Milos Gligoric
bullet_points: Proposes a novel task: retrofitting existing software code to include Exception Related Code (ERC).
The goal is to automate the tedious process of manually adding error handling (try/catch, throw statements) to large codebases.
The method utilizes Large Language Models (LLMs) guided by Exceptional Behavior Tests (EBTs) to perform the retrofitting.

stories.title: Why Is Video Still So Expensive? A Survey of Inference-Efficiency Mechanisms in Video and Audiovisual LLMs
stories.author: Mounîm A. El Yacoubi
bullet_points: Video Large Language Models (VideoLLMs) are advancing rapidly for tasks like captioning and QA.
A major hurdle is the high computational and memory cost, which scales with video length.
The survey focuses on inference-efficiency mechanisms to enable real-time and resource-constrained deployment.

stories.title: Rust is tier-1 language at Microsoft
stories.author: mmastrac
bullet_points: Microsoft has recognized Rust as a tier-1 programming language.
This indicates increasing industry adoption and endorsement of Rust within a major tech corporation.
The news signals a growing trend toward using memory-safe languages in large-scale enterprise development.

stories.title: More questions about whether researchers can trust OpenAI with unpublished math
stories.author: pred_
bullet_points: The discussion centers on the trustworthiness of OpenAI regarding unpublished mathematical research.
The topic raises concerns about intellectual property and the integrity of research shared with large AI labs.
The source material points to discussions on Mathstodon and X (Twitter), indicating a community-driven debate.

stories.title: Forgejo 16.0.4 has a critical security bug fix (RCE - Remote Code Execution)
stories.author: codeberg.org via brn
bullet_points: Forgejo, a self-hosted Git service, has released version 16.0.4.
The update addresses a critical security vulnerability.
The vulnerability is classified as Remote Code Execution (RCE), making it high-severity.

stories.title: AI Is Already Better at Coding Than Most Software Developers
stories.author: sylwia-lask
bullet_points: The article posits that AI is achieving coding proficiency surpassing many human developers.
It argues that coding itself is not the most critical skill in software development.
The piece suggests a necessary shift in focus for developers away from pure coding.

stories.title: The Verification Bottleneck in AI-Generated Software
stories.author: kenwalger
bullet_points: AI code generation speed is increasing rapidly.
The primary challenge is ensuring the correctness of AI-generated software.
The article addresses the 'verification bottleneck' in modern AI development workflows.

stories.title: Most 'AI Agents' Are Just If-Statements in a Trench Coat
stories.author: james_anderson_h
bullet_points: The article critiques the current state of 'AI Agents,' suggesting many are overly simplistic.
The author posits that many advertised agents are fundamentally just complex conditional logic ('if-statements').
It highlights a gap between the perceived complexity of agents (planners, tools) and their actual underlying mechanism.
